subject: Nuvotek competitive readout and test plan
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@nuvotek.com>, Ben Cho <ben.cho@nuvotek.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 09 Apr 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Nuvotek competitive readout and test plan

Hi Aisha / Ben — thanks again for the call today. Quick post-call recap so we’re aligned on what matters and the next steps we agreed to. I’ll loop in our delivery lead (Logan) and product lead (Camila) for scoping.

High-level customer goals (what you told us):
- Reduce inference latency to sub-40ms p95 for the 8k token readouts in your recommender flows.
- Avoid tokenized data leaving your VPC (must remain inside private deployment).
- Predictable cost per 1M tokens and ability to reserve capacity for Blackbox releases.

Top pain points called out:
- Current vendor (EdgeServe) has sporadic p95 spikes during bursts and no easy way to fall back to a smaller model without manual intervention.
- Security team requires audit logs and KMS/HSM integration before any pilot moves forward.
- Benchmarks today don’t reflect your real traffic (multi-session KV cache usage).

Decision criteria you flagged (in order):
1) Latency SLOs (p50/p95) under real traffic + deterministic fallbacks
2) Security posture (VPC + KMS, SOC2 evidence)
3) Cost per token and reserved capacity options
4) Ease of ops: rollout controls, tracing, and per-route observability

Proposed follow-ups / agreed tests:
- Redwood will run a 48-hour parity run vs EdgeServe using your sample dataset and traffic shape (we requested the sample during the call).
- Will provide a configuration matrix: batch sizes, KV cache TTLs, and quantization profiles we used.
- Deliver SOC2 summary and KMS integration doc by next Tuesday (see attachments).
- Mutual action plan: milestone dates in Drive (link below).

Attachments: redwood-demo-ops-log.csv (ops traces), redwood-security-pack.pdf (security summary).

Next actions (owners + ETA):
- Aisha: share PoC sample data + expected traffic histogram (by Mon 4/12) — ACTION ITEM
- Marissa: ship parity test config and sched (by Mon 4/12) — ACTION ITEM
- Logan: confirm resource slot for a 48-hour canary (start Wed 4/14) — ACTION ITEM
- Camila: list of evaluation probes (quality/latency/regen) + test harness (by Tue 4/13) — ACTION ITEM

Open questions we raised on the call:
- Do you need us to run tests inside your VPC or is a dedicated private deployment acceptable?
- Are there any redlines on data retention beyond the default 30-day logs?

I captured a short plan in Drive; share edits if anything is missed: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2bNuvotek-PoC-plan

Thanks — looking forward to the parity run.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-demo-ops-log.csv (CSV, 1.2MB)]
[Attachment: redwood-security-pack.pdf (PDF, 420KB)]

From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 09 Apr 2027 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Nuvotek competitive readout and test plan

Thanks Marissa — a couple of engineering clarifications from our side after listening in:

Notes:
- For parity we should match their session affinity pattern (50% long-session, 50% short) and run with KV cache warmed to typical TTLs (we should ask for a representative trace).
- We'll include two quantization profiles: int8-fp16 hybrid and full-fp16. That will show cost vs latency tradeoffs.
- Please ask Nuvotek if they can capture and share a sample of regen/follow-up prompts — quality probes need those.

Proposed test matrix (high level):
1) Baseline: EdgeServe default config (their environment) — 48h
2) Redwood config A: small batch, KV TTL 60s, int8-hybrid — 48h
3) Redwood config B: medium batch, KV TTL 300s, fp16 — 48h

Metrics to capture: p50/p95 latency, token-cost (per-1M), error/regen rate, fallback frequency, and KV cache hit ratio.

I’ll draft the exact commands and runbook for Logan to kick off; Marissa if you can nudge Aisha to upload the trace and a 1–2MB sample set today that would be great.

—Camila
Product Lead, Redwood Inference

- Timeline: we can make the environment available on Tue 4/13; prefer the parity window Wed 4/14–Thu 4/15.

We’ve also added Oak Consulting for governance oversight during the pilot.
